articles.title: Ambiguous Errors Are the Mind Killer
articles.summary: Ambiguous errors are a pervasive problem in software, representing errors that are opaque and lack clear meaning. Unlike happy-path return values, errors have long been second-class citizens across all software, with boundaries between applications and libraries, operating systems, and remote services being the primary constraints. This lack of understanding can lead to two bad options: reverse-engineering errors to understand their causes or throwing up one's hands and treating errors as if they were bombs. As a result, developers often struggle to diagnose and fix errors, and the problem is exacerbated by the viral nature of ambiguous errors, which can be difficult to resolve once they are encountered.
